messages:
maria_acme: Hey — since we enabled the int8 quant_profile on our embeddings endpoint we're seeing inconsistent vector lengths. Some calls return 1536 and others 768. This is breaking our indexer. Repro steps below.

alex_support: Thanks — that sounds bad. Can you paste a minimal repro (curl) and the model name + any headers you see (x-request-id etc)? Also did you change batching settings recently?

maria_acme: repro:
```bash
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings \\n  -H "Authorization: Bearer $API_KEY" \\n  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \\n  -d '{"model":"redwood-embed-large","input":["doc1","doc2"],"quant_profile":"int8","batching":{"dynamic":true,"max_batch_size":8}}'
```
Headers we get: x-request-id: req_0a1b2c3d, x-model: redwood-embed-large, x-model-version: auto. We started seeing it after toggling quant_profile last night.

jin_ml: Quick note: quantization itself shouldn't change embedding dimensionality. Usually dim changes mean the request routed to a different model family (e.g., redwood-embed-small=768 vs redwood-embed-large=1536). Could be a model variant mismatch in the routing layer.

tara_sre: I saw a deploy this morning: deploy-bot: rolled out quant-profile-int8-variant to region us-east-1 at 1941199000. Possibly some nodes pulled a cached model artifact with different architecture. Checking node configs + pool assignments now.

deploy-bot: rollout: quant-profile-int8-variant -> us-east-1, batch/serve nodes affected: pool-b, rollout id r-2026-04-06-09

sam_engineer: Can you try forcing single-item requests (no batching) and see if it consistently returns 1536? Also try explicit model_version instead of auto. That will tell us if dynamic batching is coalescing across incompatible variants.

maria_acme: Tried single request (one input) — got 1536. Tried batch of 2 — got [1536, 768]. When I pinned model_version: "2026-04-01-int8-v2" it returned 1536 for the batch.

alex_support: That's super helpful. Sounds like dynamic batching is combining requests served by different nodes (one node running a small architecture/variant). When we rolled the int8 artifact some worker pools may have picked up the wrong binary -> different model checkpoint.

jin_ml: Agreed. Root cause theory: the int8 rollout included an alternate distilled checkpoint (smaller dimension) for perf. The routing metadata didn't propagate capability headers for embedding dim, so dynamic batcher mixed variants. We'll add a dim capability header to model discovery so batcher refuses to coalesce differing dims.

tara_sre: For mitigation I recommend: 1) pin model_version in your request (you already did, good). 2) disable dynamic batching for now (set batching.dynamic=false) until we patch. 3) I'll cordon the affected pool nodes and redeploy consistent artifacts.

sam_engineer: Also adding quick repro command for support logs: include x-request-id from your failing batch and the raw request body. We can correlate which backend returned 768. Example:
```json
{
  "x-request-id": "req_0a1b2c3d",
  "model":"redwood-embed-large",
  "model_version":"auto",
  "batching":{"dynamic":true}\\n
}
```

maria_acme: Confirmed pinning model_version fixes it for our workload. We've switched to single-item requests for now and set a retry policy. Will wait on your patch. Thanks.

alex_support: Filing internal ticket INF-5943 to add embedding-dim to model capability headers and to make batcher validate dims before coalescing. Assigning to jin_ml + tara_sre.

jin_ml: ETA: quick guard in runtime within 24h to reject mixed-dim batches; full fix (capability advertising + rollout verification) in the next release.

tara_sre: I've cordoned pool-b and started uniform redeploy. I'll post updates to this thread when nodes finish.

maria_acme: Appreciate the fast response. We'll keep pinned version for now.

alex_support: Glad that's mitigated. Keeping this open until redeploy completes and we push the guard. Please DM me any new failing x-request-id. :thumbsup:

maria_acme: Will do. Thanks all!
